schema_note: Blocks validate against nlp_reports app/models; parameter_type, document_type, QualityAttribute criticality fields, StudyDesign and DesignSpace are local extensions (see schema_extensions_used).
schema_extensions_used: RevisionEntry / GroundTruthAnnex.supersedes (new) — the revision layer, anchored on the rendered revision-history rows
AcceptanceCriterionRecord (new) — step acceptance criteria tagged with the revision that applied them and whether they are in force or superseded
ProvenAcceptableRange (new model) — per attribute x parameter PAR, the two analyses of PCMP-001 §6.4 as the report prints them
RhetoricalSpan (new model) — argument-structure roles over the report prose
out_of_schema_notes: No set-point or NOR of the step changed at Version 2.0, so ProcessParameter.target_value and NOR are the values of the parameter table, which are also the values in force. ProcessParameter.PAR is the range carried into the control strategy: for a multivariate parameter the intersection of its NOR-propagated ranges over the outputs with a criterion (PCMP-001 §7.6), which the report states for load pH; for operating flow rate the range the report states as proven acceptable for pool host cell protein from the univariate study. rationale_for_criticality carries the classification argument of the report for the parameter, each parameter anchored on its own sentences of it.

The QualityAttribute records are the six attributes of the attribute table: the cumulative MVM clearance (assigned to the step by the register), the cumulative XMuLV clearance (a modular claim), host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A (cleared) and fragments (judged in the pool). acceptance_criteria holds the drug substance criterion and, for the four outputs with one, the Version 2.0 intermediate acceptance criterion of the step; residual DNA and leached Protein A have none at this step and are anchored on their rows of the residual DNA table. acceptance_criteria (the annex layer) holds the rows of the criteria-change table, Version 1.0 superseded and Version 2.0 in force. Step yield is a process performance attribute with no criterion: the concept attr:step_yield.

proven_acceptable_ranges: the sixteen rows of the PAR table, with par_at_setpoint and par_nor_propagated as the columns 'PAR (set-point)' and 'PAR (NOR)' print them, and the report's description of the two analyses in its own words, in report statements anchored on its sentences. The PAR of operating flow rate is not a row of that table; it is in ProcessParameter.PAR and in report statements.

The schema has no record type for a discrepancy from the plan. PD-008-01 to PD-008-10 are report statements anchored on their rows of the discrepancy register, each with the report's own sentences about it; the studies they concern carry that row as a source reference. The coding of protein load (PD-008-09) is recorded only as the report states it.

The report records no deviation: a characterization study is not GMP manufacture, so the three events of execution are study events, under the numbers Version 1.0 gave them (DEV-008-01 to DEV-008-03). They are Deviation records, the schema's only record type for an event of execution. no_impact_on_conclusions is true for DEV-008-01 (the designs were re-executed and no range, class or claim rests on the first execution) and DEV-008-03 (screening only, which sets no range), and false for DEV-008-02, which the report says can change an estimated effect and for which the record holds no data.

Studies: every row of the execution-window table with a schema study type has a StudyDesign record. The invalidated first execution S-AEX-SUP has no study type in the schema and has no record; its design matrices are report statements of Appendices A and B, and the event is DEV-008-01. Only the screening and response-surface designs carry n_runs, which the corpus test reserves for the seeded DoE designs; the augmentation S-AEX-AUG (a second block of the response-surface design) carries its runs in its rows.

StatisticalModelFit: the planned full quadratic of each output with a criterion on the planned runs and, where the augmentation measured the output, with a block term on all runs (the re-evaluation table); the selected models of the five outputs (pool host cell protein on the log scale, both LRFs on the raw scale on the planned runs, step yield and fragments with no term besides the block), each meeting PCMP-001 §7.2 as the report judges it; and the five screening models. A p-value printed as '< 0.001' has no float value; its term carries significant=true. The models within 2 AICc units and the deletions of flagged runs are report statements, one per row of their tables.

parameter_impacts_attribute: every term of a selected model with terms, on its coefficient row, with the screening effect row. The interaction of load pH and protein load in the selected XMuLV model is not asserted as an effect of protein load, because the report says it is not established as one (an explicit non-claim). parameter_does_not_significantly_impact_attribute: each parameter and output whose screening effect is not significant and whose selected model carries no term containing it, and operating flow rate on pool host cell protein and step yield from the t-tests of the flow-rate study. The screening interaction of load pH and protein load on fragments is recorded in report statements only.

The ModularContribution records are the platform claims of the step against the two cumulative requirements; cumulative_value is the sum of the platform claims the report states, not a measured clearance. The capability of the cumulative clearance is a property of the train.
The concept ids follow the Version 1.0 report and the PCP-008 Version 2.0 annex (step:aex, param:aex_*, equip:aex_sdm_column).
rhetorical_spans: authoring/rhetorical/PCR-008.spans.yaml, re-curated against the Version 2.0 text in the same pass as this builder. weak_claims is empty.

process_steps.description: Step 8 of the A-Mab drug substance process, operated in flow-through mode, the last chromatography step before virus filtration. The resin carries a quaternary amine ligand with a fixed positive charge. At the load pH the antibody carries a net positive charge and passes through the bed, while residual DNA, the acidic part of the host cell protein population, leached Protein A and virus particles bind. The column is equilibrated, loaded with the cation exchange pool adjusted to its target pH and conductivity, and chased with the first wash buffer; the pool is collected from the start of the load to the end of the chase. The register of critical quality attributes assigns to the step the cumulative MVM clearance, and it contributes a modular XMuLV claim: 5.5 log10 for XMuLV and 4 log10 for MVM.
input_materials: cation exchange pool adjusted to the target pH and conductivity of the load
equipment: scale-down model of the commercial anion exchange column

source_references.quote: The step is operated in flow-through mode and is the last chromatography step before virus filtration.
It clears host cell protein, residual DNA, leached Protein A and virus.
Anion exchange chromatography is Step 8 of the train.
The resin carries a quaternary amine ligand with a fixed positive charge.
At the load pH the antibody carries a net positive charge and passes through the bed, while species that carry a net negative charge bind.
The column is equilibrated, loaded with the cation exchange pool adjusted to its target pH and conductivity, and chased with the first wash buffer.
The step processes the cation exchange pool of a single batch at commercial scale (PCP-008 §1).

equipment.equipment_name: scale-down model of the commercial anion exchange column

source_references.quote: The studies were executed on a scale-down model of the commercial anion exchange column, qualified under SOP-1001 and operated under SOP-2011.
The model keeps the bed height, the linear flow velocity, the protein load in grams of antibody per litre of resin, and the equilibration, load, wash and chase volumes in column volumes.
The resin, the buffers and the packing method are the same as at commercial scale.
Development site | Cambridge, MA
Commercial drug substance site | Grafton, WI

parameters.rationale_for_criticality: Classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. Load pH (WC-CPP). Load pH acts on pool host cell protein and on both LRFs, with p < 0.001 in each selected model. Across its characterized range it multiplies pool host cell protein by 0.51 and raises the XMuLV and MVM LRFs by 1.24 and 1.08 log10. Its NOR lies inside every proven acceptable range. The NOR-propagated ranges for the two viruses end 0.135 and 0.1275 pH units below the NOR and 0.15 pH units above it. The other ranges span the characterized range, which reaches 0.15 pH units beyond the NOR on each side. The load is adjusted to its target pH before it is applied (PCP-008 §5.2). Load pH was classified as a WC-CPP.

parameters.rationale_for_criticality: Classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. Protein load (WC-CPP). The selected XMuLV model carries the interaction of protein load with load pH (p = 0.017), which changes the LRF across the protein load range by −0.33 to +0.44 log10, depending on load pH. That change is of the size of the repeatability of the XMuLV assay. The other XMuLV model within 2 AICc units drops the interaction, so the interaction is not established as an effect of protein load (Section 5.3.2, Section 5.3.4). The term enters the least favourable combination for XMuLV, where the margin to the claim is smallest (Section 7.2). The class of WC-CPP is a conservative judgement on that term. No effect on pool host cell protein, MVM or step yield was detected. For fragments the screening model carried an interaction of protein load with load pH (p = 0.029), and the selected response-surface model contains no term. Every proven acceptable range spans the characterized range, which reaches 70 g/L resin below the NOR and 20 g/L resin above it. Protein load was classified as a WC-CPP.

parameters.rationale_for_criticality: Classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. Operating flow rate (WC-CPP). No effect of flow rate was detected. Pool host cell protein and step yield did not differ significantly between the two ends of its range, and the spiked run at the shortest residence time met both viral claims and lay inside the prediction interval at the set-point (Section 5.4). The range proven acceptable for pool host cell protein is the characterized range, which reaches 50 cm/hr beyond the NOR on each side. For viral clearance only its upper end, 50 cm/hr above the NOR, was tested. By the rule of PCMP-001 §7.7 alone, a parameter with no demonstrated effect on a critical quality attribute would be a general process parameter. The class of WC-CPP is a judgement on the scope of the viral clearance claim. The claims of this step were demonstrated only inside the flow-rate range studied, with a single spiked run at its upper end. Flow rate could act on viral clearance through the residence time, because virus particles diffuse slowly to the ligand (PCP-008 §4.1 and §6.4). The study cannot resolve an interaction of flow rate with load pH or load conductivity, which act on clearance. Operating flow rate was classified as a WC-CPP, so that it is held within the conditions under which the claim was shown.

deviations.summary: Non-representative (deamidated) load in the first DoE execution; designs invalidated and re-executed
deviations.impact_statement: The first execution (study S-AEX-SUP) ran on load lot LOT-CEX-8842, deamidated after a hold of 36 h after neutralization, and pool host cell protein rose steeply with protein load at high Equil/Wash-1 conductivity. Both designs were invalidated under PCP-008 §7 and re-executed in full on the requalified lot LOT-CEX-8851. The data of the first execution were used only to confirm the cause; no range, class or clearance claim rests on them.

deviations.summary: Trailing-edge UV pool-collection set-point slightly permissive in both executions
deviations.disposition: corrected by modelling and verification runs
deviations.impact_statement: The trailing-edge UV set-point that ends pool collection was 180 mAU in both executions, against the corrected 120 mAU, so collection ended earlier. The set-point was the same in every run of the two executions, but a fixed UV cut can remove a different share of the trailing tail at different settings and so change an estimated effect; the record holds no data on that and does not give the set-point of the augmentation runs. The block term detected no shift between the planned and the augmentation runs. The results of the verification runs are not in the record and are not used.

deviations.summary: Equilibration/Wash-1 buffer released below its pH acceptance range on one screening run
deviations.impact_statement: The buffer lot LOT-BUF-8815 had a pH of 7.32 against its acceptance limit of 7.4. The record does not name the run, so each screening run was deleted in turn: the significant terms of pool host cell protein and XMuLV did not change, those of MVM, step yield and fragments did for some deletions. The event affected the screening design only, which sets no range; every prediction, range and judgement comes from the response-surface design.

source_references.quote: The four multivariate parameters were studied in a two-level full factorial design of 16 runs with 3 centre points, 19 runs in all (study S-AEX-SCR, 2026-03-23 to 2026-03-31).
A full factorial in four parameters estimates every main effect and every two-factor interaction without confounding, which the expected interaction of load pH and Equil/Wash-1 conductivity requires.

design_spaces.definition: The region of the four multivariate parameters (load pH, Equil/Wash-1 conductivity, load conductivity and protein load) in which every output with a criterion meets it at once, drawn on the single-batch limit (the 95 % prediction interval of a single run) for pool host cell protein and fragments and on the mean prediction for viral clearance (PCMP-001 §6.2). On a grid of 11 levels per parameter (14,641 points) it covers 95.0 % of the characterized region. MVM clearance excludes 4.96 % of the grid and XMuLV clearance 1.73 %, and pool host cell protein and fragments exclude no grid point. The excluded region lies at low load pH and high load conductivity. The whole NOR lies inside the design space, which lies inside the characterized region, the knowledge space of the study. Not confirmed at scale at its edges.

source_references.quote: The design space is the region of the four multivariate parameters in which every output with a criterion meets it at once.
It is drawn on the single-batch limit for pool host cell protein and fragments and on the mean prediction for viral clearance (PCMP-001 §6.2).
On the grid of 11 levels per parameter it covers 95.0 % of the characterized region.
MVM clearance excludes 4.96 % of the grid and XMuLV clearance 1.73 %, and pool host cell protein and fragments exclude no grid point.
The excluded region lies at low load pH and high load conductivity.
The whole NOR lies inside the design space, because every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high meets every criterion on its decision statistic ( Table 21 ).

proven_acceptable_ranges.acceptance_basis: Intermediate acceptance criterion ≤ 100 (drug substance) of PCMP-001 Version 2.0; NOR-propagated analysis judged on the 97.5th percentile of simulated batches with the other parameters drawn within their NORs, on the selected response-surface model.

statements.statement_text: Risk argument of the widening, part 1 of PCMP-001 §7.5: Who bears the risk. A widened criterion lets an upstream pool with slightly more host cell protein pass to the next step. A cation exchange pool at its widened criterion of 418 ng/mg, cleared only at the platform worst case of 4-fold, would give an anion exchange pool of 104.5 ng/mg, above the drug substance criterion. Such a batch would fail release, so for the species the release test detects the risk is the producer’s.

source_references.section_title: Verification of the platform worst case
heading_path: Verification of the platform worst case
source_references.quote: Who bears the risk.

statements.statement_text: Risk argument of the widening, part 2 of PCMP-001 §7.5: Detection. Host cell protein in the drug substance is tested at release by the ELISA AMV-3012, whose LOQ of 1 ng/mg lies far below the criterion of 100 ng/mg. The ELISA detects 80 % of the host cell protein species, as measured by 2D western blot against the platform CHO host cell protein antigen. The other 20 % are not seen by release testing either. The clearance factors of this report are measured by the same ELISA, so they do not show how the step clears those species. Nothing in the record covers them, and for that share an excursion would not be detected at release.

source_references.section_title: Verification of the platform worst case

source_references.quote: Detection.

statements.statement_text: Risk argument of the widening, part 3 of PCMP-001 §7.5: What the downstream steps must clear. Anion exchange is the last step that clears host cell protein, and no later step changes it on the platform. Under the widened criteria this step must clear at least 4.18-fold where the platform value asked for 4-fold, which is the clearance the bound shows for a single batch within the NOR.

statements.statement_text: Risk argument of the widening, part 4 of PCMP-001 §7.5: The probability that the drug substance is out of specification. In the integrated process model no simulated batch exceeded 100 ng/mg, and the tail probability of the normal distribution fitted to the batches is zero to the precision of the calculation. With no batch outside, the one-sided 95 % upper bound from the simulation is 0.15 %. It covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated process model.

concepts.canonical_name: scale-down model of the commercial anion exchange column

source_reference.quote: INV-001 found that the acceptance criteria of Version 1.0 had been set after the data were seen.
INV-002 found that the response-surface models did not meet the model adequacy criteria of the master plan.
every selected model meets each adequacy criterion of the master plan PCMP-001 §7.2 that applies to it
Pool host cell protein is modelled on the log scale and depends on load pH and Equil/Wash-1 conductivity.
Every output with a criterion met its intermediate acceptance criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high
MVM clearance bounds the design space where load pH is low and load conductivity high.
The scale-down model is qualified for pool host cell protein, the one compared output with a criterion at this step.
The bound does not depend on a single run.
It does depend on the model selection, because the plan’s full quadratic model fails the limit on overfitting.
It is also sensitive to the offset.
All five parameters were classified as well-controlled critical process parameters (WC-CPP).
The results roll up into the master report PCMR-001, which consolidates the cumulative viral clearance claim.
At the load pH the antibody carries a net positive charge and passes through the bed, while species that carry a net negative charge bind.
These limits were applied at analysis and appear in no approved plan.
The plan’s full quadratic models of all four outputs with a criterion failed its limit on overfitting.
At a higher load pH the pH lies above the isoelectric point of more of the host cell proteins, so more of them carry a net negative charge and bind.
A higher conductivity of the equilibration and first wash buffer shields the electrostatic interaction and lets weakly bound host cell protein and virus particles through.
Pool host cell protein is expressed per milligram of antibody, so a higher load raises it only where the bound impurity approaches the capacity of the ligand.
Virus particles diffuse slowly to the ligand.
This study measured fragments in the pool only, so that expectation was not tested here.
MVM is not inactivated by low pH, so this step and the virus filter carry the whole MVM claim
This step contributes one of three claims for XMuLV and one of two for MVM.
Load pH, Equil/Wash-1 conductivity and load conductivity ranked highest, because together they set how strongly an acidic host cell protein binds.
Scaling on these variables holds the residence time and the impurity mass per unit of ligand equal to those of the commercial step.
Their offset is unknown, not zero, and they are judged as the scale-down model gives them
Its criterion is met over the NOR with the offset at its estimate and at both ends of the interval, so the scale-down model is qualified for pool host cell protein.
Neither that qualification nor the bed pressure is in the record of this study
